sampling context together.

oral-bioavailability outcome.

records did not define the accepted gold outcome: never count them as extra gold
votes, and do not treat the L1/L2 name itself as a positive or negative label.

parent-condition context may apply to the query. It is not a positive-class
probability, an experimental result, or a substitute for reasoning about the
visible structure, endpoint, assay, species, formulation, exposure, and
condition. Infer direction from the record cards first, then judge transfer from
all visible context. Do not invent a numeric similarity judgment or assume that
a higher transfer_likelihood must outweigh a concrete experimental mismatch.

Use general medicinal-chemistry knowledge to interpret structures, but ground
every compound-specific empirical claim in the supplied query prior or cited
record cards. Repeated records and multiple cards from one context are not
independent evidence. Return exactly one valid JSON object and do not reveal
hidden chain-of-thought.

claims.claim: All visible L1 gold records in human or clinically relevant populations report absolute oral bioavailability at or above 24%, including aminoglutethimide ≈100% (C03), molsidomine 44–59% (C04), maraviroc 24% at 100 mg (C12), and amoxicillin 70–89% (C01, C05, C08); the only visible sub-20% record is ampicillin 12% in fasted veal calves (C17), a low-transferability species-specific result, while the same calf model gives amoxicillin 32% (C23).

The most transferable small basic-amine contexts—aminoglutethimide, molsidomine, and maraviroc—all exceed the 20% threshold, supporting that small ionizable amines can achieve F ≥ 20% despite ionization.

L3 oral-exposure records for saxagliptin, an adamantane-containing small molecule, show measurable oral AUC (AUCinf about 145–153 ng·h/mL) after single oral doses, supporting oral absorption of this structural class, though no IV comparator or absolute F is reported.

L4 Caco-2 records classify small basic amines norephedrine and cathine as highly permeable (Papp >1×10^-6 cm/s; norephedrine 10.0×10^-6 cm/s in a mixture), supporting that small ionized primary amines can still be well absorbed; this is analog evidence, not a direct query measurement.

L5 Caco-2 bidirectional transport records show that small basic amines (dexamphetamine, p-methoxyephedrine) have high A-B permeability and are not P-gp substrates (efflux ratios 0.9–1.2; no P-gp-mediated efflux with PSC-833/GF120918), and leucine is absorbed via an intestinal carrier; this supports absence of gut-wall efflux as a barrier for the query's structural class, but none of these records measure rimantadine itself.
No visible record provides affirmative threshold-relevant evidence of F < 20% for the query; the only sub-20% record (C17) is a low-transferability calf result for ampicillin.

evidence_gaps: No direct oral bioavailability or matched oral-versus-IV exposure measurement for rimantadine itself.
No direct permeability, solubility, or gut-wall metabolism measurement for rimantadine; L4/L5 records are for amphetamine analogs, Khat alkaloids, leucine, and unrelated molecules.
First-pass hepatic metabolism of the adamantane primary amine is not directly measured.
Full ionization at pH 7.4 (logD -0.82) leaves some permeability uncertainty, though small size and the lipophilic cage may compensate.
Transfer from record contexts is based on structural analogy, not identical chemistry.
content.decision_summary: Predicted high (F ≥ 20%) because all visible L1 gold records in relevant populations are positive (≥24%), the most transferable small basic-amine contexts support adequate oral bioavailability, L3 oral-exposure records add supportive but non-quantitative context, L4 Caco-2 permeability of similar small basic amines supports absorption, and L5 shows no P-gp efflux for similar small basic amines. No affirmative threshold-relevant low evidence appears; the only sub-20% record is a low-transferability calf result. Confidence remains moderate because no direct query F measurement exists and the query is fully ionized at pH 7.4.
